div.head: Quadr II 17
div.ab: Hæc de causa sanctissimi Cantuariensis archiepiscopi Anselmi cum beatissimo rege nostro Henrico et de multa Girardi uenerabilis archiepiscopi sedulitate super eam pura coram Deo ueritate collegi, sciens eum sub (absconso) clamide uirorum principum inhesisse blandiciis et ab Anglie peruersitatibus animum penitus reuocasse, cupientem exire de terra et de cognatione sua, quo dominus Ihesus euocasset, et adorare in loco ubi steterunt pedes Ejus, si pax reddetur ecclesie, si persecutio . . ., quanta si posset diligentia subuenire.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 545–546 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

div.ab: These things concerning the case of the most holy archbishop of Canterbury Anselm with our most blessed King Henry, and concerning the great zeal of the venerable Archbishop Gerard in it, I have collected in pure truth before God, knowing that he had clung under a (hidden) cloak to the flatteries of princely men and had wholly recalled his mind from the perversities of England, desiring to go out from his land and from his kindred, whither the Lord Jesus should call him forth, and to worship in the place where His feet stood, if peace should be restored to the Church, if persecution . . ., to give aid with as much diligence as he could.
